experiment.objective: Determine whether traffic signals adapt through local positive feedback by measuring changes in green light duration at a specific intersection during morning rush hour
experiment.procedure: 1. Select two comparable intersections, one with adaptive signals and one with fixed-time signals. 2. Measure baseline green light duration, queue length, and throughput for both intersections over 5 days. 3. Monitor adaptive intersection for 30 days, recording green light duration and traffic metrics daily during 7-9 AM. 4. Maintain fixed-time intersection as control with constant 60-second green lights. 5. Control for external factors by monitoring weather, accidents, and construction. 6. Compare green light duration changes between adaptive and fixed intersections.
experiment.expected_result: Adaptive intersection shows 15-25% increase in green light duration over 30 days while maintaining or improving throughput, while fixed intersection shows no change.
experiment.falsification_condition: No statistically significant increase in green light duration at the adaptive intersection after 30 days of operation under consistent traffic conditions
experiment.sample_requirements: Two comparable intersections with similar traffic patterns, vehicle detection sensors, data logging equipment
safety_constraints: Traffic control personnel present during monitoring
experiment.information_gain: Confirmation or refutation of adaptive traffic signal hypothesis, with potential implications for smart city traffic management systems
